raw_case_text: The present case report is about a 32-year-old man who was referred to our hospital from rural area with malaise, fatigue, weight loss and fever on examination, the patient was found to be breathless at rest, with pedal edema, tender hepatomegaly, pulsatile precordium, jugular venous pressure raised and murmurs of mitral regurgitation and aortic regurgitation and a 3 month history of rigors. Chest roentgenogram showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions. Over the next few hours rapid deterioration with respiratory failure secondary to pulmonary edema led to him being intubated. Laboratory investigations revealed low hemoglobin 9 g/dL and normal aspartate aminotransferase (19 U/L; upper normal limit [UNL] 40 U/L), alanine aminotransferase (30 U/L; UNL: 40 U/L) and gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (34 U/L; UNL 37 U/L). Electrocardiography was normal with sinus rhythm, and radiography revealed normal cardiac silhouette. Serum agglutination tests were positive (titer > 1:2000) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay tests for anti-Brucella immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M antibodies were strongly positive (124 U/mL and 35.5 U/mL; UNL 30 U/mL and 20 U/mL, respectively). In addition, Brucella melitensis were isolated from two of three consecutive blood cultures. Trans-esophageal echocardiography was performed to investigate for the possible presence of Brucella-related complication of endocarditis because of our patient's diastolic and systolic heart murmur, positive blood cultures. The transesophageal echocardiogram also noted a 2 x 1.5 cm posterior aortic root abscess and a 1 mm defect between the main pulmonary artery and the ascending aorta. The echocardiography showed native aortic valve endocarditis, large vegetation; aortic ring cavity and abscess [Figures 1 and 2] also, there was moderate pericardial effusion without signs of cardiac tamponade. Dilatation of left ventricular cavity with a preserved ejection fraction of 55%, three cusped aortic valve, a large mobile vegetation on right and left aortic cusp [Figure 3]. Our patient was given oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily plus oral Rifampicin 900 mg once daily for 7 days, with intramuscular streptomycin 1 g once daily for the first 3 weeks. On the 10th day of treatment surgery was performed with aortic valve replacement (no. 21, Carbomedix). We performed aortic annular skeletonization by dissecting all infectious and necrotic tissue within the abscess cavity and the fistula between the ventriculoarterial junction and the Sino tubular junction. The completely resected annular area was covered with a fresh autologous pericardial patch that was sutured firmly to fibrous tissue, for a secure proximal anastomosis as described by Keles et al. Reconstruction performed using a fresh pericardial patch and aortic valve replacement with a Carbomedix 21 prosthetic valve. The antibiotic regimen was continued after the operation and blood cultures after 1 month of operation were sterile. The patient was followed-up for 2 months with oral antibiotics and warfarin. After the procedure warfarin was started. The patient is still being followed-up in a healthy condition after the 3th month since diagnosis and treatment with oral antibiotics and warfarin when last seen, 12 months after starting therapy; our patient was well with no sign of relapse. Careful medical literature searching revealed that our case is the only reported case of aorto pulmonary fistula following Brucella aortic endocarditis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old male presented with malaise, fatigue, weight loss, fever, rigors for 3 months, and acute breathlessness at rest.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed malaise, fatigue, progressive weight loss, fever, and rigors over a 3-month duration. Upon referral, he was breathless at rest and rapidly deteriorated over several hours into acute respiratory failure secondary to cardiogenic pulmonary edema, requiring emergency endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of a rural area. Prior medical comorbidities, prior surgeries, and specific animal/dairy exposures not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Malaise, fatigue, weight loss, fever, 3-month history of rigors, breathlessness at rest. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Breathless at rest, intubated and mechanically ventilated. Cardiovascular: pulsatile precordium, elevated jugular venous pressure, murmurs of mitral regurgitation and aortic regurgitation. Abdomen: tender hepatomegaly. Extremities: bilateral pedal edema.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL; AST: 19 U/L (UNL 40 U/L); ALT: 30 U/L (UNL 40 U/L); GGT: 34 U/L (UNL 37 U/L). ECG: normal sinus rhythm. Chest radiograph: normal cardiac silhouette, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates consistent with pulmonary edema, and bilateral pleural effusions.
objective.advanced_workup: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE): native trileaflet aortic valve endocarditis with large mobile vegetations on the right and left aortic cusps; 2 x 1.5 cm posterior aortic root abscess cavity and aortic ring abscess; 1 mm fistula/defect between ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery (aorto-pulmonary fistula); dilated left ventricular cavity with preserved ejection fraction of 55%; moderate pericardial effusion without tamponade physiology. Surgical intervention: emergency median sternotomy with aortic annular skeletonization, radical debridement of infectious/necrotic tissue from the abscess cavity and ventriculoarterial-sinotubular junction fistula, reconstruction with fresh autologous pericardial patch, and mechanical aortic valve replacement (No. 21 Carbomedics).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Brucella native aortic valve infective endocarditis complicated by aortic root ring abscess, aorto-pulmonary fistula, severe aortic and mitral regurgitation, and cardiogenic acute pulmonary edema.
Confirmation: Brucella melitensis isolated from 2 of 3 consecutive blood cultures; serum agglutination test positive at titer >1:2000; ELISA positive for anti-Brucella IgG (124 U/mL, UNL 30) and IgM (35.5 U/mL, UNL 20).
Differentials ruled out: Non-brucellar bacterial endocarditis ruled out by blood cultures yielding B. melitensis; primary cardiomyopathy ruled out by valve destruction and fistula.
Treatment & Outcome: Preoperative and postoperative antimicrobial therapy with oral doxycycline (100 mg BID) plus oral rifampicin (900 mg daily) for 7 days, combined with intramuscular streptomycin (1 g daily) for the first 3 weeks, followed by oral antibiotics and anticoagulation (warfarin) for 2 months postoperatively. Repeat blood cultures at 1 month were sterile; patient fully recovered and remained well without relapse at 12-month follow-up.
